questions.q: What does the phrase discipline equals freedom mean in the summary?
a: Self-control is the path to the freedom you want
Rules at work give you more personal time
Discipline removes the need for any planning
Freedom means doing whatever you feel like
questions.why: The overview explains that financial, physical, and time freedom all come through disciplined habits.

questions.q: According to Willink, what is the only shortcut that actually works?
a: Giving up the search for fast fixes
Finding a mentor who has done it before
Working in short, intense bursts
Buying tools that save time and effort
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the one real shortcut is dropping the attitude of looking for quick fixes.

questions.q: Why is getting up early described as a keystone habit?
a: One early win makes later wins more likely
It gives you more hours than other people have
It replaces the need for exercise and diet
It guarantees you will never feel tired
questions.why: Lesson 2 says the win of rising early makes it easier to stack other good choices later in the day.

questions.q: What does Willink advise if you need more sleep after a short night?
a: Take naps rather than sleeping in
Sleep in until you feel fully rested
Skip the alarm and reset your schedule
Go to bed much earlier the next evening
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to keep the wake-up time fixed and recover with naps instead of sleeping late.

questions.q: Who does the summary say is the only person worth competing against?
a: Your former self
Your closest colleague
The best in your field
Your younger sibling
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that the most rewarding victories are the ones you win against who you used to be.
